answer.headline: At CHS, official enplanements compounded at {F48} a year from CY2011 to CY2019; the latest full-year change was {F54}.
answer.body:
Assumption: Charleston is Charleston International Airport (CHS). Official ACAIS calendar-year boardings are the annual enplanement series. T-100 segment enplanements are a separate observed measure, used here for the monthly trend and for full-year CY2024 and CY2025. ACAIS does not include CY2021, CY2022, or CY2023, so annual growth in those years is not established.

Published ACAIS levels at CHS were {F1} in CY2011, {F9} in CY2019, and {F10} in CY2020. After the unpublished years, CY2024 was {F44} and CY2025 was {F45}.

Calculated ACAIS changes versus the prior published year were {F66} in CY2012, {F67} in CY2013, {F68} in CY2014, {F69} in CY2015, {F70} in CY2016, {F71} in CY2017, {F72} in CY2018, {F73} in CY2019, {F51} in CY2020, and {F54} in CY2025. The compound annual growth rate from CY2011 to CY2019 is {F48}. The endpoint compound rate from CY2019 to CY2025 is {F57}, and from the CY2020 level to CY2025 is {F60}. Those endpoint rates cross the unpublished years. They are not a year-by-year path, and they are not the latest annual change.

T-100 enplaned passengers at CHS were {F61} in CY2024 and {F62} in CY2025, a calculated change of {F65}. Over {F42.period}, the descriptive monthly linear trend is {F42}. The latest month versus the same month a year earlier ({F43.definition}) changed by {F43}. The monthly series runs from {F11} ({F11.label}) to {F41} ({F41.label}). CY2026 is only partly inside that window, so an annual CY2026 growth rate is not established.

claims.text: Official ACAIS enplanements at CHS were {F1} in CY2011, {F9} in CY2019, {F10} in CY2020, {F44} in CY2024, and {F45} in CY2025.

Calculated ACAIS year-to-year changes at CHS were {F66} for CY2012, {F67} for CY2013, {F68} for CY2014, {F69} for CY2015, {F70} for CY2016, {F71} for CY2017, {F72} for CY2018, {F73} for CY2019, {F51} for CY2020, and {F54} for CY2025. The CY2011-to-CY2019 compound annual growth rate is {F48}.

T-100 enplaned passengers at CHS were {F61} in CY2024 and {F62} in CY2025, a calculated change of {F65}. Over {F42.period} the calculated monthly linear trend is {F42}, and the calculated change for {F43.definition} is {F43}.

The latest observed annual growth is the small CY2024-to-CY2025 change ({F54} on ACAIS and {F65} on T-100). {F60} compounds the move from the CY2020 ACAIS level {F10} to the CY2025 level {F45}, and {F57} compounds the move from the CY2019 level {F9} to CY2025. Both endpoint rates cross years with no ACAIS observations, so they do not establish the annual path or the current run-rate.

assumptions: Charleston is bound to Charleston International Airport (CHS) in Charleston, SC, because entity resolution returned an exact city match for that airport. Yeager Airport (CRW) in Charleston/Dunbar, WV, and the Charleston-Huntington-Ashland combined statistical area are other name matches and are excluded.

Annual growth is taken from official ACAIS calendar-year boardings where those years are published. The monthly trend and the CY2024-versus-CY2025 passenger change use T-100 segment enplanements. The two measures are reported separately and are not treated as interchangeable.
limitations: ACAIS returns out_of_coverage for CY2021, CY2022, and CY2023, so annual growth inside that span is not established. Endpoint compound rates that cross the gap use only the endpoints.
T-100 in this trend covers {F42.period}. CY2026 is incomplete there, so an annual CY2026 total and growth rate are not established.
The monthly linear trend includes seasonality and is descriptive. It is not a seasonally adjusted annual growth rate.

T-100 counts a connecting passenger at each enplanement. ACAIS is official calendar-year revenue passenger boardings. Neither series measures terminal capacity, fares, profitability, or unmet demand. These figures are not a forecast and not a valuation.
